previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted with acute right upper quadrant pain and nausea. Initial evaluation revealed gallstones, gallbladder wall thickening, and elevated liver enzymes, consistent with acute cholecystitis. A HIDA scan confirmed non-filling of the gallbladder. After failing conservative management, he underwent a laparoscopic cholecystectomy on hospital day three. Postoperatively, he developed transient urinary retention requiring a short-term catheter and mild postoperative ileus, both of which resolved. His white blood cell count normalized, and cultures were negative. Diuretics were held perioperatively and restarted before discharge. He recovered well, tolerated a regular diet, ambulated independently, and was discharged home on postoperative day six with follow-up arranged. His liver disease and HCC remained stable throughout the admission.

Brief Hospital Course:
This is a ___ yo M with HCV and alcoholic cirrhosis who presents 
with abdominal pain, diarrhea, and fever 4 weeks after 
laparoscopic cholecystectomy with concern for gallbladder fossa 
abscess, found to have C diff colitis.
.
1. Clostridium diff Colitis: The patient had been recently 
treated with ABX for wound site infection following lap 
cholecystectomy. The patient was seen at an OSH ED with nausea, 
abdominal pain, diarrhea, and fever. He was transfered here for 
possible gallbladder fossa abscess/fluid collection. While here, 
he had a C diff toxin that was positive. He was started on 
treatment with IV Flagyl. The IV flagyl was switched to PO 
formulation. The patient tolerated this well, but he continued 
to complain of diffuse, lower abdominal pain, and frequent 
stooling. Over his hospital admission, the patient had fewer 
bowel movements. He still complained of slight pain after 
eating, but otherwise was asymptomatic. The patient was 
discharged on a 14 day course of PO Flagyl 500mg TID. 
.
2. S/P Cholecystectomy: The patient had a laparoscopic 
cholecystectomy performed on ___. His post-op course 
was complicated by ileus and wound site infection. The wound was 
opened and packed and he was treated with ABX. In the hospital, 
he had no pain at the surgical site. The site was CDI without 
drainage. An US of the abd/gallbladder was negative for fluid 
collection in the gallbladder fossa. The surgical team did not 
believe there was any concern for infection. 
.
3. EtOH Cirrhosis: The patient had no signs of decompensation on 
this admission. His nadalol and spironolactone were continued.
.
